description: HeurChain: Two-Tier Consolidating Memory for AI Agents — heuristic chaining for persistent agentic memory with hippocampal-inspired consolidation
summary: HeurChain gives a fleet of agents a shared two-tier memory — a 7-day working vault that auto-promotes into a Redis long-term store, searched with BM25 rather than a vector pipeline — which is the kind of local-first, observable design I actually trust instead of bolting on another embedding service. The hippocampal-consolidation framing isn't just branding; the tier-promotion rule is a concrete mechanism that maps cleanly onto how I'd want PenguPool's parallel sessions to share context without each one re-deriving the same facts, and the agent-agnostic HTTP/MCP surface means AgentOn Pocket and a Claude Code session on my laptop hit the same store with zero per-agent config. Setup is a single `docker compose up` plus a URL the agent reads from the README or a bundled JSON to self-wire, which shaves off the last bit of glue-toil I usually spend when I stand up a new agent loop.
